_spec: BANZA v1.0.0 L0 independent-implementation trial - adversarial input set
_derivation: Every case is derived from a rule the frozen package states. Where the specification determines a verdict the case carries must_reject:true and cites the rule; where it does not, the case asserts only that the implementation is well-behaved and repeatable. Inventing a verdict the specification does not require would test this harness's opinion rather than BANZA.
_bar: no crash, no hang, deterministic across repeated runs, no silent repair. A rejection is a valid, well-behaved outcome everywhere in this set.
_note_on_vector_gap: ADV-001 to ADV-004, ADV-008 and ADV-009 exercise P8 (input form), which the specification states but the committed conformance vectors do not cover. They are trial artifacts and do not alter the normative surface; the gap is recorded as a pre-trial finding.

cases.title: unpaired high surrogate in a member value
cases.basis: spec/canonicalization.md P8 — text containing an unpaired surrogate MUST be rejected before canonicalization begins

cases.title: invalid UTF-8 byte sequence
cases.basis: spec/canonicalization.md P8 — text that is not valid UTF-8 MUST be rejected; it is not repaired, replaced or substituted

cases.title: top level is an array, not an object
cases.basis: spec/canonicalization.md P8 — a canonicalizable artifact MUST be a JSON object at the top level

cases.title: truncated JSON text
cases.basis: spec/canonicalization.md P8 — text that is not well-formed JSON MUST be rejected

cases.title: duplicate member appearing far apart in a large object
cases.basis: spec/canonicalization.md P3 — the same member name more than once, at any nesting level, MUST cause rejection. The two occurrences are separated so a last-wins parser cannot mask the defect by proximity.

cases.title: integer one above the safe upper bound
cases.basis: spec/canonicalization.md P2 — integers MUST be within +/-(2^53-1); out-of-range values MUST be rejected, fail-closed

cases.title: deeply nested object
cases.basis: no depth limit is stated in the frozen package, so no verdict is determined. The bar is that the implementation neither crashes nor hangs, and answers the same way twice.

cases.title: empty input
cases.basis: spec/canonicalization.md P8 — empty text is not well-formed JSON

cases.title: byte-order mark before the object
cases.basis: spec/canonicalization.md P8 — a BOM is not part of well-formed JSON text. An implementation that strips it silently is repairing input, which P8 forbids.

cases.title: NUL character inside a member value
cases.basis: no rule in the frozen package forbids U+0000 in a string, and RFC 8785 escaping determines its output form. No verdict is determined, so the bar is well-behavedness.

cases.title: very long member name
cases.basis: no length limit is stated in the frozen package. The bar is that a long name is handled deterministically rather than truncated or rejected inconsistently.

cases.title: member names differing only by Unicode normalisation form
cases.basis: spec/canonicalization.md P5 — no Unicode normalisation is performed and verifiers MUST NOT normalise. The two names are distinct members, so this is not a duplicate and MUST NOT be rejected as one.
